title: Today Overview
bestFor: See today's calendar and overdue reminders without changing anything.
prompt: Tell me today's calendar events and overdue reminders. Do not change anything.
safety: Read-only. It only reads Calendar and Reminders and never writes data.

title: Daily Briefing
bestFor: Start the day with calendar, reminders, mail, and recent notes.
prompt: Brief me on today's calendar, overdue reminders, unread mail, and recent notes.
safety: Read-only by default. Saving a note or reminder becomes a separate approved action.

title: Inbox Triage
bestFor: Turn mail backlog into a small, reviewable set of follow-up tasks.
prompt: Find emails from Alex about the project and create reminders for action items.
safety: Reads mail first; reminder creation is a per-call write path and stays auditable.

title: Meeting Prep
bestFor: Collect the context you need before the next meeting.
prompt: For my next meeting, find related notes, contacts, files, and reminders.
safety: Read-only prep flow. Creating agendas or tasks is an explicit follow-up write.

title: Project Digest
bestFor: Summarize active project context across indexed Apple workspace data.
prompt: Summarize what changed since yesterday on my current project.
safety: Digest is read-only after indexing; indexing writes only to Taxi's local semantic store.

title: Focus Blocks
bestFor: Turn open reminders into calendar time blocks.
prompt: Plan focus blocks for today's open reminders, but ask before creating each event.
safety: Calendar event creation is non-destructive but non-idempotent; each event is auditable.

title: Research to Output
bestFor: Move from Safari, files, and notes into a draft note or email.
prompt: Open the Apple developer docs in Safari, summarize the page, and draft a note.
safety: Reading and summarizing are read-only. Sending or saving output is a separate write action.

title: Development Window Check
bestFor: Compare a selected development app or Simulator window with an expected screen state.
prompt: Check the expected screen state of my development app. Ask for the app/window and expected state if missing. Run setup_permissions with system_only true; if Screen Recording is denied or unknown, explain the reported recovery steps and stop. List windows with captureTargets true. If multiple windows match, ask me to select one. Pass all three fields of its target (windowId, ownerPid, title) to capture_window. On a stale target, list again and confirm the selection. Compare the returned image with the expected state and report observed evidence, uncertainties, target, timestamp, and hash. Capturing an image alone does not verify the result.
safety: Requires Screen Recording and the active runtime approval policy. Target selection and image comparison happen in the connected AI client. Configuration readiness does not verify permissions, capture, or the expected state.
